content_html:
Morphic Fields vs Dependent Origination

Both frameworks emphasize relationality and continuity over isolated essences. Morphic fields posit a real, non‑local field that carries habits; dependent origination rejects any hidden substrate and explains continuity by causal interdependence and emptiness.

Aspect Morphic Field Dependent Origination Alignment
Definition Invisible, formative fields that shape and transmit habits/forms across space & time. Principle that all phenomena arise in dependence on conditions; no inherent essence. Both reject isolated essences; one posits a field, the other a logic of conditionality.
Role of Memory Memory is non‑local via resonance with past patterns. Memory/continuity arise from causal chains (body, mind, karma, culture) without a storage “substance”. Both broaden “memory” beyond local storage.
Mechanism Hypothesized morphic resonance (contested empirically). Causal interdependence; emptiness denies a substrate or hidden medium. Divergence: substrate‑like field vs. non‑substantialist causality.
Transmission / Continuity Habits spread and ease recurrence across populations. Continuity because conditions interpenetrate; nothing arises in isolation. Both describe continuity without fixed identity.
Ontology Suggests real, non‑local fields in nature. Emptiness (śūnyatā): phenomena exist conventionally, lack inherent nature. Divergence: field‑substance vs. anti‑essentialism.
Metaphor “Memory‑field” shaping organisms & culture. “Indra’s Net”: infinite mutual reflection/interconnection. Both use imagery of interconnection; different commitments.
Aim Explain regularities beyond genetics / learning orthodoxy. Soteriological: insight into interdependence / emptiness to alleviate suffering. Divergence: empirical‑explanatory vs. liberative‑philosophical.

Notes

  • Use “Indra’s Net” as a conceptual metaphor for non‑atomistic memory without committing to a physical field.
  • When invoking Sheldrake, clearly separate metaphor from mechanism and flag mainstream critiques.
